evidence_items.locator: Section 3, opening paragraph; dataset description in section 2
evidence_items.explanation: The paper describes roughly 180 million tokens of GPT-3.5-generated coding exercises and an improvement from 29% HumanEval accuracy for the base model to 50.6% after fine-tuning. This is useful learning from substantial model-generated content.

evidence_items.publisher: Ilia Shumailov and colleagues via arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: Recursive training experiments support the possibility of degradation when generated content dominates successive training datasets. They establish a harmful regime, not that every substantial synthetic dataset is useless.

evidence_items.publisher: Matthias Gerstgrasser and colleagues via arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Introduction, discussion of accumulating versus replacing data

receipt.public_excerpt: model collapse is avoided when accumulating data

evidence_items.explanation: The experiments distinguish recursive replacement from accumulation alongside original real data. Avoiding collapse does not itself prove improvement, but it undermines the proposed inevitability of harm.

unresolved_gaps: These experiments do not determine the effects of every synthetic-data mixture or long-term web contamination.
